name: onesie-stream
description: Use when onesie runs over more than one record, a JSONL file, a list of lines or saved request bodies, and before writing a shell loop that calls onesie once per record. Also when reading onesie output with jq, when the input is live such as tail -f, or when a batch run exits 6 or 3.
compatibility: Requires the onesie binary on PATH.

rules.short: Read the error before you read any answer.
rules.why: A failed record still prints a line, carrying an error rather than answers. A missing field reads as null in `jq`, and null sorts below every number, so a threshold check with `<` silently admits a failed record as if it had passed. The error sits at `.error`, but under `--merge` it sits at `.answers.error`, or under the `--merge-key` name, since the input's own fields stay at the top. In `-o csv` and `-o tsv` it is the `error` column, empty on a row that answered.
rules.bad: onesie --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl < in.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.urgent.value < 0.8)'
rules.good: onesie --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl < in.jsonl | jq -c 'select(.error == null and .urgent.value < 0.8)'

rules.short: Match output line N to input line N, unless the exit code says the run stopped early.
rules.why: Output keeps input order under any `-j`, so line N answers record N. A failed record still gets its line, and so does a blank line in jsonl or lines unless `--skip-blank` drops it. A blank line in csv or tsv is skipped with no output line. Under `-i lines` each `-o json` or `-o values` line carries `line`, its input line number from 1, which counts the blank lines `--skip-blank` drops, so match on it under `--unordered` or `--skip-blank`. Under `--merge` it sits inside the answers object, as in `.answers.line`. Some stops leave only a prefix of the input: an auth failure, exit 3, `--stop-on-error` with the failing record's code, or 6 for a line onesie could not read, `--stop-on-assert`, exit 1, or 6 when an earlier record failed, an interrupt, exit 130, a csv row over the length limit or an input column that clashes with an output column, exit 2, and a consumer that closes the pipe, such as `head`, which exits 0. A csv or tsv header that is not valid exits 2 before any line. `--unordered` drops the ordering for throughput.

rules.short: Under --merge read answers from .answers, and rename it with --merge-key if the record has one.
rules.why: Answers sit at the top level keyed by question id. `--merge` folds them under an `answers` key instead, and `--merge-key` renames that key, which matters when the record already has one called `answers`. Folding only means something in a structured output, so `-o table`, `-o raw` and `-o markdown` are rejected under `--merge`.

rules.short: On live input, filter each line on its answer, since a stream's exit code arrives only at the end.
rules.why: A stream exits once its input ends, with 1 when any assertion was false, and `tail -f` never ends. So nothing chained after it with `&&` or `||` runs, and `-q` is refused on a stream with exit 2 anyway. Act on each line as it arrives instead: under `--assert` every record carries its gate result at `.assert`, true or false, and under `--merge` at `.answers.assert`. Pass `jq --unbuffered` so each match leaves jq at once rather than when a buffer fills. A failed record carries `.answers.error` under `--merge` and no `assert`, so a filter on `.answers.assert == false` alone skips it. Route it too, as the good example does, since a record with no answer is not an all clear.
rules.bad: tail -f app.log | onesie 'does this line report a failure a person must act on' -i lines --assert 'answer.value < 0.8' -q && page_on_call
rules.good:
tail -f app.log | onesie 'does this line report a failure a person must act on' \
    -i lines --merge -o json --assert 'answer.value < 0.8' \
  | jq -c --unbuffered 'select(.answers.assert == false or .answers.error != null)'

rules.short: Freeze a run with --print-request and replay it with -i request.
rules.why: `--print-request` over a stream writes one body per input line, and `-i request` reads those bodies back. It checks that each line is one JSON object and still applies the flag rules, but nothing inside the body: no question checks, no normalization and no policy. So a bad body is sent as is and comes back as an error record, not an exit 2, and a good one comes back as the raw response body, not the usual record. A response that is not a System One result, or whose answers do not fit the body's questions, is an error line of kind response instead. The one change is a body whose `model` is missing, empty, all whitespace or null, which takes the run's resolved model. Under `-i request`, `--print-request` prints each body as it would be sent, so adding it to a pipeline turns the whole run into a dry run: `onesie --ask urgent='is this urgent' -i jsonl --print-request < in.jsonl > bodies.jsonl && onesie -i request < bodies.jsonl`.

rules.short: Read csv or tsv with -i and write it back with -o csv --merge.
rules.why: `-i csv` and `-i tsv` read a header row and send each row as an object keyed by it, so a question can name a column such as `body`. A byte order mark before the header is dropped, and a blank or repeated column name exits 2. A csv field may be quoted to hold commas and newlines. TSV has no quoting: a quote is ordinary text and every non blank line is a row. `-o csv` and `-o tsv` write one header row: the input columns under `--merge`, an `id` column under `--id`, one column per question holding its `-o values` answer, followed by an `ID_fallback` column for a question with a fallback, holding `low_confidence` or `error` when the fallback replaced the answer and empty otherwise, an `assert` column holding `true`, `false` or `abstain` when there is an assertion, empty on a failed row, and an `error` column. In `-o tsv` a tab or line break inside a cell becomes a space. Under `--merge`, an input column named like a question id or `error`, or `assert` under a gate, exits 2 at the first row. An input `id` column never clashes. `--merge` into `-o csv` or `-o tsv` needs csv or tsv input, since jsonl has no fixed columns, and both refuse `--usage`, and `--merge-key` even beside `--merge`.

rules.short: Write -o markdown for a PR comment or a job summary, and never as a file to resume or parse.
rules.why: `-o markdown`, or `-o md`, writes a stream as one GitHub table with a summary alert. A table cannot be read back into answers, so `--resume`, `--merge`, `-r` and `-q` exit 2. Read answers with `-o json` or `-o csv`. A GitHub comment holds at most 65536 characters, so send a large stream to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` or write it as csv. The rest is under Streams in [REFERENCE.md](https://github.com/frodi-karlsson/onesie/blob/main/REFERENCE.md#streams).
rules.bad: onesie 'is this urgent' -i jsonl --id '.id' -o markdown --out answers.md --resume
rules.bad_unverifiable: the checker strips -o, --out and --resume before every dry run, so it cannot observe this refusal

rules.short: Choose the state with --map and name each record with --id.
rules.why: `--map EXPR` is a jq expression whose result is the state, so `--map '.body'` keeps a customer name away from the model. Drop every field that does not bear on the question, such as a timestamp or an order id, since each one adds noise to the answer. `--id EXPR` names each record on every output line, and `--resume` skips by it. Keep it a cheap field lookup that yields one string or number, unique per record. A record whose map or id fails gets an error line, and the stream carries on. The rest is under Streams in [REFERENCE.md](https://github.com/frodi-karlsson/onesie/blob/main/REFERENCE.md#streams).

rules.short: Write a long stream with --out and rerun it with --resume and --id after a failure.
rules.why: Pass `--resume` from the first run, since a missing or empty `--out` file starts fresh. After a failure, rerun with the same `--out` and `--id`: the run skips every id the file answers and asks the rest, failed records included. `-j`, `--timeout` and `--retries` may change between runs. Exit 2 names what changed, such as the model or `--map`, so put it back, or drop `--resume` and start over. A record whose content changed under the same id keeps its old answer. The rest is under Streams in [REFERENCE.md](https://github.com/frodi-karlsson/onesie/blob/main/REFERENCE.md#streams). A full resume: `onesie 'is this urgent' -i jsonl -j 8 --map '.body' --id '.id' --out answers.jsonl --resume < tickets.jsonl`.

rules.short: Dedup shares a request within one run, --cache shares it across runs, and --resume skips the ids an --out file already answers.
rules.why: Within one stream, records whose request is identical, the same state after `--map`, the same questions and the same model, are asked once, and each still gets its own line. `--no-dedup` asks every record, and `--stats` counts the records deduplicated. That lasts one run. `--cache`, or `ONESIE_CACHE=1`, keeps each successful response on disk, so a later run asks nothing for a request it has seen, whatever the record's id. `--resume` with `--id` goes by id, not by request: it skips every record whose id the `--out` file already answers, even one whose content changed, and asks the rest. So finish a run that stopped with `--resume`, and rerun records you edited with `--cache`, which asks only the ones that changed.
